column1: # Call-count fingerprint groups: NAME <TAB> PATTERN[|PATTERN...]
# One row per logical component. The patterns are plain SUBSTRINGS of a mangled symbol name,
# matched against both engines' callgrind profiles and summed per side; `|` separates
# alternatives, and a row normally carries one alternative per language because rustc and
# clang do not name the same function the same way. Each row is the claim "rfish calls this as
# many times as Stockfish does" -- a claim about the ALGORITHM, not about cost.
# A row whose pattern matches NOTHING on one side is a MISS and FAILS. A silent zero would
# read as agreement forever, which is precisely what an inlined-away symbol produces. If a
# compiler change inlines one of these, fix the row -- prefer a callee too big to inline over
# its caller -- and never delete the check.
# TWO ROWS HAVE ALREADY BEEN MOVED THAT WAY, both after a refactor in this tree rather than a
# compiler change, and the weekly lane reported both as MISS on 2026-08-10:
#   do_move   `do_move_checked` became a one-line wrapper over `do_move_recording` when threat
#             recording landed, and the search calls the recording form DIRECTLY. The wrapper
#             inlines to nothing; the callee counts every make-move on every path and matches
#             upstream exactly (163345).
#   evaluate  `eval::evaluate` inlines into `SearchWorker::evaluate`, and that wrapper is
#             itself inlined at THREE of its six call sites -- it reports 35771 against
#             upstream's 62975, so a caller symbol cannot carry this row at all. The forward
#             pass every static evaluation runs can: `LayerStack::propagate` is 62975, and it
#             is a different symbol from the one `nnue_network` reads, so the two rows still
#             fail independently. Put the row back on the entry if rustc ever stops inlining
#             it -- an entry count is the claim this row would rather make.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. Every other differential in this tree compares values: the bench anchor,
# the goldens, nnue-check, upstream-nodes. Each passes over a state divergence that happens
# not to move a number on the positions it drives. Two real defects were found by this and by
# nothing else, both in how a move is RENDERED for output:
#   * the PV reporter walked a cloned position, playing every PV move to name the next, and
#     truncated the line at the first move that failed a legality check. Upstream renders
#     against the root and prints the stored line whole.
#   * `bestmove ... ponder X` named the ponder move in the position AFTER the best move,
#     cloning and playing it first. Upstream names it against the root.
# Together, 1492 position clones and 1492 do_move/undo_move pairs per `bench 16 1 8` that
# upstream does not perform, and a PV that could come out shorter than upstream prints it.
# Every value gate was green through both.
movepick_next
search_node
qsearch
evaluate
nnue_network
update_quiet
do_move
pseudo_legal
# NOT GATED, and the reason is measured rather than assumed.
# A call count is inlining-immune at the CALLEE -- it does not care how the callee was
# reached -- but only while the callee itself survives as a symbol on both sides. Upstream is
# clang with `-flto=full` plus PGO, and it inlines these four INTO the search templates, so
# its symbol counts omit every inlined site. rfish keeps them as calls.
# The proof is internal to upstream's own profile and needs no second measurement: upstream
# reports do_move 163345 and undo_move 68736 over the same bench. Every do_move in a search is
# undone, so upstream's true undo_move count IS 163345 and the symbol is short by 94609 --
# those calls were inlined away. rfish reports 163331, which is the number a consistent count
# looks like. Gating these would assert that two compilers inline identically, which is not a
# fact about this port.
#   undo_move
#   legal
#   gives_check
#   see_ge
# If a future change gives upstream a non-inlined symbol for any of them -- or gives rfish an
# `#[inline(never)]` reason of its own -- move the row up rather than leaving it here.
